dataset.name: Pyrogenic Organic Matter Laboratory Experiment: Aerobic Respiration and Geochemistry from Variably Inundated Stream Sediments
description: This dataset supports a broader study examining the effects of variable inundation and pyrogenic organic matter on ecosystem respiration. The dataset provides data generated from a laboratory batch experiment investigating the interaction between variable inundation conditions (wet and dry sediment) and pyrogenic organic matter (burned and unburned treatments). The contents include time series dissolved oxygen, sediment geochemistry data, and field metadata (including qualitative information on instream and river corridor characteristics). Additional data types, including respiration, will be added as they become available.
For details on how to navigate data packages generated by this project, see https://data.ess-dive.lbl.gov/portals/PNNLRiverCorridorSFA/About.

In addition to a readme, this data package also includes a file-level metadata (FLMD) file that describes each file and a data dictionary (DD) that describes all column/row headers and variable definitions.

This dataset is comprised of (1) file-level metadata; (2) data dictionary; (3) field metadata; (4) international generic sample number (IGSN) mapping file; (5) readme; (6) field protocol; (7) sample name metadata; (8) an environmental context picture for the dry and inundated sampling locations; and (9) a subfolder with sample data from the sediment incubation experiment. The sample data subfolder contains (1) dissolved organic carbon (DOC, measured as non-purgeable organic carbon, NPOC); (2) total nitrogen (TN); (3) gravimetric moisture; (4) carbon dioxide; (5) field wet sediment mass, dry sediment mass, water mass, and field wet sediment volume in incubation and sediment NPOC/TN vials; (6) methods codes; and (7) raw time series dissolved oxygen and temperature. All files are .csv or .pdf.

measurementTechnique: Sediment samples were collected from the Columbia River at locations with contrasting inundation conditions – field wet sediments that had been continuously inundated for several months and field dry sediments from a higher elevation on the same shoreline that had been dry for several months. Site metadata, including general environmental information, were manually recorded in the field. See YEP_Sampling_Protocol.pdf for details on sample collection and site metadata collection. Briefly, sediment samples were sieved to less than 2 millimeters and transported on blue ice to Pacific Northwest National Laboratory where they underwent a 7-day pre-incubation period in an environmental chamber to allow stabilization to laboratory conditions. After the pre-incubation period, sediment incubations were conducted using three treatments: (1) synthetic Columbia River water (0 mg C/L) as a negative control, (2) unburned Douglas fir leachate at 9 mg C/L, and (3) burned (high severity) Douglas fir leachate at 9 mg C/L. All treatments were applied to both field wet and field dry sediments. Aerobic respiration rates were calculated from the slope of the linear regression between dissolved oxygen data measured using FireSting oxygen probes and incubation time. Incubations were monitored continuously with measurements every 5 seconds, with experiments ending after 6 hours or when dissolved oxygen levels reached 2.0 mg/L. For details regarding laboratory and instrument methods, see the alphanumeric methods codes located in the header rows of the chemistry data csv file and their associated definitions in YEP_Methods_Codes.csv. Data formats follow ESS-DIVE Reporting Formats.
